analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Feyenoord (25 pts, one behind PSV) host Excelsior (15th, 11 pts), who have lost five league games in a row and failed to score in their last four. Feyenoord are winless in five in all competitions after a 5-3 loss at Heerenveen, so Giovanni van Bronckhorst needs a response. St. Juste is out longer (counted) and Zinhagel has a hamstring injury; Anis Hadj Moussa is the big doubt, with reports split between an ankle sprain and a dispute in the Algeria camp, and Van Bronckhorst does not want to risk him, so 17-year-old Jerayno Schaken could make his first start. Excelsior's Nesto Groen is banned (counted) and Feyenoord loanees Sliti and Plug should play. The numbers add a big derby boost for cards, but this is a friendly city derby: Feyenoord are holding a 'Rotterdam Day', opening the sector barriers and letting Excelsior fans mix with home fans; referee Robin Hensgens is average.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already counting Excelsior's collapse (22 conceded in six), St. Juste's absence and Groen's ban. Feyenoord's patched defence has conceded in five straight games, but they may lose their most dangerous winger Hadj Moussa to a teenager making his first start, and Excelsior have not scored in four league games; those pull both ways, so I drop yesterday's small lean and stay at 3.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Feyenoord taking most of them (6.8) and Excelsior's drop in corners already in the momentum adjustment. Without Hadj Moussa Feyenoord still have Valente and Schaken or Nelson wide, and they will have most of the ball either way, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, and that already includes a +39% derby boost plus referee Robin Hensgens' average record. This is not a hostile derby: the clubs share loan players (Sliti, Plug), Feyenoord have opened the sector barriers and let Excelsior fans sit among home fans for a 'Rotterdam Day', and a game with Feyenoord on the ball brings few home fouls. I trim a little more than yesterday, -8% to about 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 19.2 and Excelsior on just 9.1 after a dismal run (45 shots in six, already counted). Feyenoord need a win and will dominate the ball, which is already the numbers' expectation, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already including Excelsior giving up many on-target shots and barely hitting the target themselves (9 in six). Groen is banned and Sliti should play, so Excelsior's threat stays small, as the numbers already assume; I stay at 10.9.
